title: Adaptive payload sharding and priority windows for multi-sink audit forwarding
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Problem: External SIEM and webhook sinks vary widely in throughput and semantics (ack patterns, payload size limits, TCP timeouts). Our current single-stream forwarder can cause head-of-line blocking, large retries, and tenant-level unfairness when a single slow sink or large event stalls delivery. Goal: implement an adaptive sharding + prioritized retry window model so that audit events are sliced, routed, and retried with tenant-aware priority while preserving ordering guarantees where required and providing cryptographic delivery verification for external sinks.
proposed_solution: 1) Payload sharding: slice oversized audit batches into shard segments with per-shard sequence marks and a shard-level HMAC. 2) Priority windows: maintain short (0-5s) and long (5-60s) retry windows per tenant+sink so high-priority control-plane events are retried aggressively while low-priority analytics events use exponential backoff. 3) Multi-sink routing: allow parallel fanout to multiple sinks with independent shard trackers to avoid head-of-line blocking. 4) Signed delivery verification: include a signed verification token in forwarder metadata; sinks that support handshake will return signed acknowledgements which we reconcile for proof-of-delivery. 5) Per-tenant backpressure shaping and a local DLQ with replayable, idempotent records and compacted retention for compliance replays.
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests demonstrating shard reassembly correctness for payloads up to 16 MB split into shards <= 1 MB
SLO: 99.9% of P0 admin events acknowledged or retried within 10s under a simulated slow-sink scenario (200ms per request + 5% failure rate)
Observed reduction in head-of-line blocking in e2e load test by >= 60% compared to baseline
Proof-of-delivery flow implemented and validated with at least two external SIEM adapters (Splunk HEC and Datadog webhook) returning signed acks
Console UI exposes per-tenant priority window controls and a roll-forward toggle; rollouts gated behind security review
implementation_steps: Design doc: finalize shard envelope format and HMAC fields (link below)
Runtime: implement sharder/unsplitter in forwarder pipeline with configurable max_shard_size and max_inflight_shards
Routing: add priority window controller and tenant-scoped quotas in front of fanout stage
Adapters: update Splunk and Datadog adapters to parse shard envelopes and return signed ack when configured
DLQ: implement tenant-scoped persistent DLQ with replay API and idempotency keys
Observability: add metrics for shard success/failure, per-sink queue depth, and proof-of-delivery verification rate
E2E tests: chaos tests simulating slow sinks, partial acks, and network partitions
Console: small UI to set per-tenant priority windows and view verification status
Rollout: dark launch followed by canary to 5 tenants, then staged ramp conditioned on metrics
risks: Increased complexity in forwarder pipeline may add CPU overhead and GC pressure; need to quantify on smaller instances
Sinks that do not support signed ack will require fallback: potential mismatch between our perceived delivery and real delivery => require clear SLAs and doc for customers
Sharding introduces reassembly latency; if mis-configured, could worsen tail latency for small events
Cross-tenant ordering guarantees tradeoff: to avoid unfairness we may relax strict ordering for non-control-plane events. This is a product decision that affects some compliance customers
notes: Datadog webhook changes: patch series available in repo under adapters/datadog/shard-support
Security review scheduled: 2026-01-28 with security-eng and compliance teams
comments: 2026-01-19 - Aisha Gomez: Scoped MVP to support two priority classes (control, default) and two retry windows to keep initial complexity low.
2026-01-22 - Liam Park: Implemented initial shard envelope prototype; observed ~8% CPU increase on dev forwarder under baseline load. Need perf bench before canary.
2026-01-24 - Nora Chen (Security): Requested threat model for HMAC key management and KMS integration; added to design doc.
2026-01-26 - SRE (comment): Need circuit-breaker thresholds for sinks that start giving malformed acks to avoid wasting retries.
2026-02-01 - Product (Jamal Ortiz): Product approved relaxing ordering for non-admin events; admin events must preserve order and get priority treatment.
2026-02-03 - Liam Park: Added per-tenant backpressure shaping and DLQ prototype; starting integration tests this week. Updated estimate remains 5 points.
test_plan: Unit tests for shard/envelope encoding and HMAC verification
Integration tests with stubbed Splunk/Datadog adapters that simulate delayed and partially-successful acks
Load tests: 100k events/s with mixed sizes to validate head-of-line reduction and CPU impact
Chaos: introduce sink-level network partitions and validate DLQ + replay correctness
Security test: key rotation test for HMAC keys via KMS; verify no data loss on rotation
rollout_plan: Dark launch: enable shard mode in staging for internal tenants only for 24h
Canary: enable for 5 small tenants (non-PII workloads) for 72h and monitor verification rate and error budgets
Ramp: 25% tenant rollout for 7 days if canary stable; otherwise rollback and debug
General availability: enable by default but opt-out for customers requiring strict legacy ordering; provide migration guide
migration_notes: Existing webhook configs will continue to work in compatibility mode. Customers that opt-in to signed-ack must update their sink implementation or enable our adapter proxy. Provide migration runbook and contact path to SEs for enterprise tenants.
security_considerations: HMAC keys will be stored in KMS; forwarder will fetch short-lived signing keys and rotate periodically. Signed-ack verification must be enforced in high-security tenants. We must also ensure audit events preserved for compliance replays even when verification fails (store unverified events in DLQ).
